BIOEFFECT EGF Serum (night) is preservative-free and passes the post-procedure test. EGF Day Serum contains phenoxyethanol and does not. Same brand, same active, same ladder.

Ladder rungs are not interchangeable on attributes other than strength. The ladder_id grouping must not imply substitutability — it groups related products so completeness can be checked, not so members can be moved between them freely. Worth an explicit note before any substitution logic is written.

ladder_id groups rungs so completeness can be checked, but two findings showed rungs are not interchangeable: BIOEFFECT night is preservative-free and post-procedure eligible while its day serum is not, and Crystal Retinal 1 carries the same coumarin, tonka and vanilla as Crystal Retinal 20.

A substitution_blockers field now derives, per rung, which attributes differ from verified siblings — post-procedure eligibility, allergen load, niacinamide, mechanism, photosensitivity tail. Rungs with fewer than two verified siblings are marked NOT ASSESSABLE rather than defaulting to safe, because a silent pass is how substitution logic causes harm.
Substitution derivation over-claimed on rinse-off products

The first run labelled differing preservative status as a POST-PROCEDURE ELIGIBILITY difference on the benzoyl peroxide WASHES. Preservative status genuinely differs there, but post-procedure eligibility is a leave-on concept — a cleanser is rinsed off within a minute.

Corrected to PRESERVATIVE STATUS for rinse-off formats. Sixth time inspecting derivation output caught an error the code did not — the standing check after every derivation change is earning its keep. Leave-on versus rinse-off is itself a missing attribute worth adding, since several rules (post-procedure eligibility, cumulative exposure, photosensitivity) apply differently.
application_format added and dependent rules re-run
Four rules already depended on whether a product stays on the skin — post-procedure eligibility, cumulative exposure, acid contact time and substitution safety — and none could see it.
Derived across all finished products. Post-procedure eligibility is now explicitly leave-on only. Substitution blockers re-derived with format included, and format difference is itself now a blocker.
The AHA tail is retained on rinse-off products, deliberately

A rinse-off AHA has far shorter skin contact than a leave-on acid, so effective exposure is lower. But the mandated sunburn alert with its one-week tail is printed on rinse-off products too — CeraVe Acne Control Gel and the FAB KP scrub both carry it.

The tail is retained and annotated rather than reduced. The labelled warning is not conditional on format, and inferring a shorter window from contact time would be Substrate substituting its own reasoning for mandated labelling — exactly the move the regulatory review exists to prevent. Note it as a candidate for clinical refinement, not an engine decision.
The closest product in the database to the Substrate thesis

Alastin Restorative Neck Complex's stated mechanism is clearing degraded elastin and collagen from the ECM and supporting new synthesis, with flax seed extract included specifically to raise endogenous hyaluronic acid. That is the estrogen → HAS2 → tissue HA → ECM integrity chain, applied to the neck and décolleté where oestrogen-related laxity presents earliest in a perimenopausal population.

Worth an explicit entry in the Hypothesis Library rather than sitting as a product note. It is also the natural candidate for an outcome-tracking pilot, since the claimed mechanism and the founding hypothesis are the same chain and the anatomical site makes change visible.
TriHex Technology is not a fixed composition

TriHex resolves to three declared peptides in the Neck Complex (palmitoyl hexapeptide-12, palmitoyl tripeptide-1, acetyl tetrapeptide-2) and two in Regenerating Skin Nectar (palmitoyl tripeptide-1, palmitoyl hexapeptide-12).

A branded technology name does not guarantee a fixed formulation across a line. Any actives-library entry for TriHex must be per-product. Worth checking the same for other branded complexes in the database — Proxylane, Matrixyl 3000, Cell-Ox Shield, EnviroScreen, Path-3.
A reformulation that removes four fragrance molecules and a dye

NEOSTRATA Triple Firming Neck Cream: the prior formula ends with ethylene brassylate, methyldihydrojasmonate, isobutyl methyl tetrahydropyranol and methyl decenol, plus caramel and Yellow 5. The current formula is marketed fragrance-free and adds MicroDiPeptide229 and bakuchiol. Both are on sale under the same name.

The most consequential reformulation found in this work for a reactive population — a member avoiding fragrance and dyes gets opposite answers depending on the jar. Fragrance analogue of the gluten finding at REV-0306. Confirm the changeover date; reformulation flags need a resolution date, not just a note.
A topical product claiming to target adipose tissue

Revision states Nectifirm ADVANCED 'targets adipose tissue'. Master 18 (Dermal Adipose / Facial Volume) is the least populated master in the database and the one whose evidence table was recovered from extraction artifacts.

A topical adipose claim is a strong claim and sits directly on the facial-volume thesis. Log in the Hypothesis Library with an explicit evidence grade, and route the CLAIM to Dr. Bentley as an example alongside the Sunday Riley hormonal-acne claim at REV-0338 — both are language Substrate must not reproduce even when quoting a brand.
Premium neck creams for mature skin carry fragrance

Nectifirm ADVANCED contains Fragrance (Parfum) and lemon peel extract; the prior NEOSTRATA formula carried four fragrance molecules and a dye. Both are premium, dermatologist-distributed and aimed at mature skin.

Seventh instance of positioning and composition diverging, and the pattern now has a shape: the products aimed at the oldest, most reactive users are among the most heavily fragranced. Worth a systematic sweep of every SKU tagged mature or sensitive against its declared allergen load.

42 merged duplicate tombstones and 2 unidentifiable rows moved to a new Retired_Records sheet. Before deletion, every tombstone was checked programmatically: canonical target present, and the merged row's master membership carried into Product_Master_Links. All 42 passed.

Products_Canonical now contains only rows that represent something real. The verification check ran BEFORE the deletion rather than after — the same discipline that REV-0359 showed was missing when a merge was marked resolved without being executed. Source lines are preserved in Retired_Records so any import can still be traced back.
Two rows retired as permanently unidentifiable

SKP-0147 (recovered name "Revision Revox Line Relaxer" contradicted by value-tier and copper-peptide attributes) and SKP-0298 (both Aquaphor and Vaseline present in its fields, both already canonical elsewhere). Neither could be resolved from internal evidence, and the source markdown was never available in this work.

Retired rather than left flagged in the product table. An unidentifiable row sitting among real products is a standing risk of eventually being verified against the wrong thing — which is the specific failure the whole extraction audit existed to prevent. If the source is recovered, rebuild them from it.
Third-party accreditation is stronger evidence than a free-from claim

Vichy Minéral 89 and Tower 28 SOS both hold the National Eczema Association Seal of Acceptance. That is external assessment, unlike the self-declared free-from claims this work has repeatedly found contradicted by the printed INCI — seven instances so far.

Capture accreditation as an attribute distinct from brand claims. Given how often free-from wording has proved unreliable here, an externally assessed seal is one of the few sensitivity signals that does not need checking against the ingredient list.
A barrier-repair serum with alcohol third and parfum last

La Roche-Posay Hyalu B5 is positioned as repairing and refilling the skin barrier and is widely recommended for compromised and ageing skin. Its list runs Aqua, Glycerin, Alcohol Denat., and ends with Parfum.

Eighth instance of positioning diverging from composition. The contrast with Vichy Minéral 89 is unusually clean — same category, same channel, similar price, half the ingredients, no fragrance, no alcohol, eczema-association seal. For a reactive member the ranking is not close and is invisible from either product's marketing.
Every limb of the Substrate thesis appears in one product

SkinCeuticals H.A. Intensifier Multi-Glycan claims to amplify the skin's OWN hyaluronic acid by 30% — an endogenous-synthesis claim — via Proxylane acting on HA and dermatan sulfate and a postbiotic ferment acting on glycosaminoglycans, and is positioned explicitly for use after dermal fillers.

Natural first test case for outcome tracking, and simultaneously the sharpest evidence-grading problem in the database: the claim is exactly what Substrate would want to be true, which is when an independent grade matters most. The 30% figure is brand-run and single-source. Grade the MECHANISM separately from the PRODUCT — Proxylane's effect on GAG synthesis is researchable independently of this marketing.
Thirteenth extraction artifact, fifth distinct detector failure
"Approved / Investigate" — a status-column value in Master 18. Every detector passed it because both words are capitalised, satisfying the proper-noun test.

Move to Evidence_Fragments. Five distinct failure modes now: keyword lists, entity-type exclusions, annotations in name fields, multi-value cells, and capitalised status values. The lesson is not to build a sixth heuristic but to rebuild the import with typed columns.
Study population is a selection criterion, and only one retinoid has a matching one

Avène cites clinical data for RetrinAL 0.1 in women averaging 47 years and in a 44-woman study aged 45–65. No other retinoid in this database cites a study population matching Substrate's members — the rest report all-adult or unstated cohorts.

Capture study population as an attribute. For a platform defined by a life stage, evidence generated in that life stage is a stronger signal than concentration, and it sits ABOVE strength in the ladder-selection ordering established at REV-0344. Worth auditing every clinical claim already captured for the population it was generated in.
Three retinaldehyde ladders now make the selection rule usable

Medik8 Crystal Retinal (0.01–0.2%, coumarin/tonka/vanilla at every rung), Geek & Gorgeous A-Game (0.05–0.1%, no fragrance materials), Avène RetrinAL (0.05–0.1%, thermal spring water base, hypoallergenic, age-matched clinical data).

Same active, three formulation philosophies, three tolerability profiles. The rule "select the ladder on tolerability, then the rung on strength" now has three real options to choose between rather than two — which is what makes it a decision rather than a fallback.
RetrinAL 0.1 sold under two names at two prices

Bluemercury lists 'RetrinAL 0.1 Intensive Cream' at $79 and 'RetrinAL 0.1% Intensive Multi-Corrective Cream' at $68 under the same UPC. The Multi-Corrective adds niacinamide and hyaluronic acid to the original Relastide/Pre-Tocopheryl formula.

Reads as a reformulation sold under both names simultaneously. The niacinamide addition matters — it would newly trigger the exclusion at REV-0201 for a member who tolerated the older version. Confirm which is current.
Clinical evidence population audited across every captured claim

Of the finished products in this database, 4 carry a clinical claim whose study population is age-matched to Substrate's members, 21 state an age outside that range, 1 carry a clinical claim with the population unstated, and 165 carry no captured claim at all.

The unstated group is the important one: brands cite participant counts far more often than they cite who the participants were. For a platform defined by a life stage that is the difference between evidence and marketing. Capture study population at verification going forward, and treat unstated as a distinct state from absent — not as a pass.
Only TWO products have age-matched clinical evidence

The first run classified four products as age-matched. Two of those — Avène Tolérance (19–57) and EltaMD Skin Recovery (24–56) — are broad adult cohorts that merely SPAN the perimenopausal window rather than being recruited in it. After refining to require a narrow range centred in the window, only SkinCeuticals C E Ferulic (40–60, n=50) and Avène RetrinAL 0.1 (average 47, n=23) qualify.

Two products out of 191. That is the honest state of age-matched evidence in this database, and it is a finding about the CATEGORY rather than about the data collection — brands overwhelmingly do not recruit in this population. It is also a defensible reason for Substrate to generate its own outcome data: the evidence gap is real and nobody else is filling it. Seventh time inspecting derivation output caught an over-claim in my own logic.
State-matched evidence is a second, better class for the procedure wedge
Cicaplast Lips was tested on the lips of subjects taking isotretinoin — a maximally compromised barrier, and the hardest lip case there is. That is not age matching; it is STATE matching.

The audit at REV-0388 found only two products with age-matched evidence. This suggests a second axis that may matter more for procedure prep and recovery, where the question is tolerance on damaged skin rather than efficacy on intact skin. Capture state-matched evidence (post-procedure, post-laser, isotretinoin, eczema-flare, radiotherapy) alongside study population — a perimenopausal member post-procedure is defined by her skin state as much as her age.
A near-anhydrous formula with no preservative system

Water sits twelfth of fifteen ingredients and there is no preservative in the list — consistent with a lipid system that does not need one. It would satisfy the anhydrous branch of the post-procedure test at REV-0339.
Fourth product to satisfy the post-procedure rule, and the first in a lip/perioral format. Relevant because perioral is a common post-procedure site and the database held almost nothing for it.
Salicylate/aspirin allergy — a hard contraindication not previously captured

Paula's Choice states plainly that anyone allergic to aspirin (acetylsalicylate) should not use products containing salicylic acid. That is a cross-reactive allergy with no tolerance override, and it applies to every BHA product in the database. Derived across all of them: 17 products carry a functional salicylate (salicylic acid or a salt), 15 carry a salicylate ester or botanical salicylate.

Two tiers deliberately, not one. Free salicylic acid and its salts are the established cross-reactive risk. Butyloctyl and ethylhexyl salicylate appear across the sunscreen master as emollients and UV boosters, and willow bark appears in several products — cross-reactivity there is far less established, so flagging them at the same severity would make the gate unusable. Surface the second tier only for a member with a confirmed aspirin allergy.
Body BHA exposure and the AHA/BHA distinction

A 2% BHA applied daily over the whole body is a larger total exposure than any facial product in the database — the same point as AmLactin at REV-0302. But this is a BHA, so the AHA seven-day photosensitivity tail does not apply, even though the brand still directs SPF 30+.

Good test of the two rules interacting correctly: body-surface exposure scales up, photosensitivity does not attach. Both hold independently, and an engine collapsing them would get one of the two wrong.
Master 15 is a technology master — grade the enzyme, not the product

Plankton Extract (photolyase), Arabidopsis Thaliana Extract (photolyase) and Micrococcus Lysate (UV endonuclease) appear together in Photozyme DNA Youth Recovery and skinbetter Alto, and Plankton Extract alone drives both ISDIN Eryfotona products. Four products, three brands, one shared enzyme set.

The differentiator between these products is the surrounding formulation, not the active. Grade the ENZYME CLASS once in the Hypothesis Library and let all four inherit it, rather than grading four products separately against the same literature. This is also what the Master 18/15 evidence table recovered from the extraction artifacts was structured to ask.
DNA-repair enzymes are licensed materials, so analogues can exist

Unlike Melasyl and Thiamidol, which are single-company actives with no generic equivalent (REV-0253), photolyase and endonuclease preparations are licensed raw materials available to multiple brands. skinsort's comparison engine already names Aspect Skincare Super PD Complex at an 80% ingredient match to Photozyme.

Fourth category in which the REV-0256 boundary holds: low-cost analogues are findable where the active is commodity and impossible where it is proprietary. That boundary is now tested across vitamin C, retinoids, pigmentation and DNA repair — enough to build the capability on.
Three undeclared acids in a barrier-repair moisturiser

Skinbetter Trio is explicitly positioned to hydrate a COMPROMISED BARRIER and contains salicylic acid (28th), phytic acid (39th) and lactic acid (43rd, final). None appears in the brand key-ingredient list.

At those positions they are pH adjusters, so the AHA photosensitivity tail correctly does not fire. But the salicylate allergy gate has NO dose threshold — a cross-reactive allergy does not care about position. A member with an aspirin allergy must be flagged here, in a product she would be steered toward precisely because her barrier is compromised. Seventh hidden-acid case and the one with the most consequence.
Chirality is a sixth potency determinant, and the only one not in the INCI

Face Reality specifies chirally correct L-mandelic and L-lactic acid rather than racemic mixtures. Chirality affects enzymatic interaction, but no other product in this database declares it and INCI nomenclature does not require the prefix.

Joins concentration, acid identity, pH, salt form and delivery system. Unlike all five of those, it CANNOT be derived from a standard ingredient list — so capture it where a brand declares it and treat it as unknown otherwise, never as assumed racemic. A rare case where the data simply is not available from the label.
Fourteenth unversioned name — Face Reality mandelic ladder
Face Reality sells 5%, 8% and 11% L-Mandelic Serums as separate SKUs. The source name gave no strength.
Scoped to the 8% as the brand's stated gold standard, with ladder_id assigned so the other two rungs can be added. Sixteenth ladder in the database.
A reformulation that changed the DIRECTIONS, not just the formula

The prior version of The Ordinary Salicylic Acid 2% Solution was directed for morning and evening use. The current one is once daily in the evening and adds an explicit contraindication the older listings do not carry: do not use on sensitive, peeling or compromised skin.

Every reformulation flagged in this work so far has been compositional. This one changes what the member is told to do and adds a hard exclusion — and a database tracking only INCI changes would have logged it as minor (witch hazel out, saccharide isomerate in) and missed the important part. Version-track directions and contraindications separately from the ingredient list.
A brand-stated exclusion for compromised skin

The brand states the product must not be used on sensitive, peeling or compromised skin — which includes post-procedure. This is unusually direct for a consumer brand and is stated in the directions rather than buried in a warning.

Directly relevant to the procedure wedge: this is the inverse of the post-procedure eligibility rule at REV-0339. Products that are explicitly CONTRAINDICATED on compromised skin should be flagged as strongly as those that are eligible — the engine needs both poles, not just the permitted list.
A pigmentation product whose irritants cause the thing it treats

PCA Skin Pigment Gel Pro carries alcohol second and witch hazel water third, plus rose flower oil. Hyperpigmentation-prone skin is by definition prone to inflammatory pigment responses — post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation is the mechanism the product exists to prevent.

Ninth positioning-versus-composition finding and the most nearly self-defeating. The brand also names pigmentation from HORMONAL CHANGES explicitly, which is melasma in a perimenopausal population — Substrate's exact territory. Pair against the low-constraint options at REV-0254; this sits at the opposite end of the tolerability range from Alastin A-Luminate and Cyspera.
Copper in a barrier moisturiser blocks vitamin C layering
Prequel Multi-Quench contains copper gluconate at position 13, present as a trace mineral rather than an advertised active. It cannot be layered with the eight L-ascorbic acid products in Master 05.

Exactly the case the derived chemical_incompatibility field exists for — nothing about the product suggests it, and no member would think to check a barrier moisturiser for a vitamin C conflict. Ester forms of vitamin C are unaffected, a distinction the rule already encodes.
Two of three externally accredited products are hypochlorous sprays

Prequel Universal Skin Solution holds the National Psoriasis Foundation Seal of Recognition, joining Tower 28 SOS and Vichy Minéral 89. Both hypochlorous products also satisfy the post-procedure eligibility test and trip no exclusion gate in this database.

A convergence worth noting: the simplest chemistry, the external accreditation and the post-procedure eligibility all land on the same small set of products. For the reactive and post-procedure segments, hypochlorous sprays look like the structurally safest category rather than merely an option within it.
Post-procedure is at least two states, not one

The Biocellulose Masque packaging says both: suitable after laser, microneedling, dermabrasion, IPL and chemical peels, AND only apply on HEALED skin. Alastin Regenerating Skin Nectar and the two hypochlorous sprays are formulated for the immediate open-barrier phase; this masque is for recovery once re-epithelialisation is complete.

Everything built around post-procedure eligibility (REV-0339) has treated it as a single state. Split the flag into IMMEDIATE-POST and RECOVERY before it drives any recommendation — a product safe in one phase is not automatically safe in the other, and the immediate phase is far more constrained. This gives the procedure-phase attribute at REV-0277 a brand-stated boundary rather than an inferred one.
Second state-matched clinical claim, and the first for procedure recovery
Packaging states the masque is clinically tested for use after laser, microneedling, dermabrasion, IPL and chemical peels. That is evidence generated in the exact state Substrate's wedge addresses.

Follows Cicaplast Lips (REV-0391), which was tested on isotretinoin-compromised lips. Two state-matched products against two age-matched ones (REV-0388) — the state axis is looking at least as productive for the procedure wedge, and worth auditing for deliberately rather than noticing case by case.
Periorbital substantiation is now three of five

Ourself Advanced Regenerative Eye Serum states dermatologist, clinical and ophthalmologist testing, and its directions name the upper eyelids explicitly. It joins Colorescience Total Eye and La Roche-Posay Toleriane Dermallergo Eye on the substantiated side; Supergoop Bright-Eyed and The Ordinary Caffeine Solution remain unsubstantiated.
Better than the one-of-three position first recorded at REV-0349. The gate is usable rather than merely restrictive — it excludes a minority of the eye master, not the whole of it.
Copper peptide and vitamin C advertised in the same formula

Third-party analysis identifies copper tripeptide-1 in Ourself's eye serum, while the brand simultaneously advertises stabilised vitamin C. If that vitamin C is an ester form there is no conflict; if it is L-ascorbic acid the two inactivate each other.

Second time the co-formulated-versus-layered distinction (REV-0221) has arisen inside a single product rather than between two. Resolve against the printed INCI. The engine needs to distinguish which vitamin C form is present before firing or suppressing the copper rule — form matters more than presence.
Both Regimen Lab products are unverifiable for the same reason
Level Serum and Vitamin X (SKP-0096) both have third-party ingredient counts but no published INCI from any retailer or the brand.

Two of two makes it a brand-level distribution signal, not two coincidences. A brand whose ingredient lists no reseller publishes is a brand Substrate cannot ground recommendations in. Decide whether to carry Regimen Lab at all before spending further verification effort.

Every finished product in Products_Canonical now carries a resolved status. 154 verified or partially verified, 3 explicitly not verified with reasons recorded (2 Regimen Lab on brand-level source failure, 1 Photozyme Reset with no source located).

The three unverified rows are recorded as decisions rather than gaps. Batch 2 scope: the outstanding INCI pulls flagged on partially-verified records, the Rx and exosome rulings, and the structural items in this queue.

The last two were added 2026-09-05. Only "Finished Product" and "Multi-step System / Kit" should ever enter the INCI verification queue.

Derived from the INCI. Values seen: Free AHA, AHA salt, BHA, BHA salt, PHA, Enzymatic, Retinoid. Resolves REV-0203 and REV-0307 — "exfoliant" and "antioxidant" as single categories cannot carry correct rules.
Free acid vs Salt (buffered). A salt delivers less free acid at equal stated percentage — REV-0301.
Populated only where published. Null is common and must be handled explicitly, not treated as average — REV-0294.
Water-free construction. Determines post-procedure eligibility and removes the need for preservatives — REV-0276.
User-activated products whose composition differs before and after mixing — REV-0282.

Days of post-cessation photosensitivity. Set to 7 where a free AHA or AHA salt is present at exfoliating position. NOT set for BHA or enzymatic products, and NOT triggered by citric acid as a buffer — REV-0288 as refined by REV-0291 and REV-0305.
Twelve rows recovered from Products_Canonical that were evidence-table cells, not products. Rebuild the underlying appraisal tables here rather than in the product database.

Derived from INCI. Chemical incompatibilities have NO tolerance override — the actives cancel each other regardless of skin robustness, which is different in kind from an irritation warning. Currently covers copper peptides x L-ascorbic acid and benzoyl peroxide x L-ascorbic acid. Note ester forms of vitamin C (THD ascorbate, ascorbyl glucoside, 3-O-ethyl) are NOT affected and must not be caught.

Secondary market or legacy formulas, separated by "||". Kept OUT of ingredient_list so that position-based derivation reads one formula only. Regional variants are not alternatives to reconcile — both are correct, for different bottles.
Which market the ingredient_list describes. Required wherever variant_formulas is populated.

Product IDs a review item acts on. Required on every item marked RESOLVED so the resolution can be checked mechanically against the data. Added after REV-0359 found a merge marked RESOLVED that had never been executed and that no sweep could detect, because the item described its effect in prose.

Groups products that are strength or format rungs of one brand line. Makes ladder completeness checkable directly instead of being inferred from name similarity — which could not detect a ladder missing an endpoint, the case that matters most. ALSO protects ladders from the fuzzy duplicate sweep, which flags siblings as high-similarity pairs and must never merge them (REV-0330).

For each ladder member, which attributes differ from its verified siblings — post-procedure eligibility, fragrance allergen load, niacinamide, mechanism, photosensitivity tail. Exists because ladder_id groups products for completeness checking and must NOT be read as substitutability. Rows with fewer than two verified siblings are explicitly marked NOT ASSESSABLE rather than defaulting to safe.

Leave-on / rinse-off / timed mask / stick-patch / photoprotective. Derived from product name and manufacturer directions. Load-bearing for post-procedure eligibility (leave-on only), cumulative exposure, acid contact time and substitution safety. Where directions are unverified the value is marked inferred rather than asserted.

Rows removed from Products_Canonical: merged duplicates whose canonical target and master memberships were verified present first, and rows that could never be identified. Source lines preserved so an import can be traced. Nothing here should re-enter the product table without being re-derived from source.

The population a captured clinical claim was generated in. Four states: age-matched to the perimenopausal range, age stated but outside it, claim captured with population unstated, and no claim captured. Exists because for a life-stage-defined platform, WHO the evidence came from matters as much as what it showed — and the audit found the age-matched case is rare.
